```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(knitr)
is_pdf  <- knitr::is_latex_output()
is_html <- knitr::is_html_output()
# Table style for PDF tables (greyskull; "classic" changes nothing).
raisins_tstyle_knitr_hook(params$table_style)

# The PDF font twins (Caladea, Gelasio, ...) have no Greek glyphs, so in PDF
# Greek letters are written as LaTeX math, which renders in any font.
pdf_text <- function(x) {
  if (!is_pdf) return(x)
  x <- gsub("\u03b1", "$\\\\alpha$", x)
  x <- gsub("\u03c4", "$\\\\tau$", x)
  x
}
markdown_text <- function(value) {
  vapply(value, function(x) {
    chars <- strsplit(x, "", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
    punctuation <- grepl("[[:punct:]]", chars)
    chars[punctuation] <- vapply(chars[punctuation], function(ch) paste0("&#", utf8ToInt(ch), ";"), "")
    paste0(chars, collapse = "")
  }, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
}

tbl <- function(d, cap, key) {
  if (is.null(d) || !nrow(d)) return(invisible(NULL))
  align <- ifelse(vapply(d, is.numeric, logical(1)), "r", "l")
  d <- gre_table_cells(as.data.frame(d), params$digits)
  if (is_html) {
    print(kableExtra::kable_classic(
      kable(d, format = "html", caption = cap, row.names = FALSE, align = align),
      full_width = FALSE, html_font = params$font))
  } else if (is_pdf && !identical(names(d), c("Item", "Detail"))) {
    # Keep natural table size and shrink only when the table is wider than the page.
    pages <- split(seq_len(nrow(d)), ceiling(seq_len(nrow(d)) / 20))
    for (rows in pages) {
      table <- kable(d[rows, , drop = FALSE], format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE,
                     row.names = FALSE, align = align)
      cat("```{=latex}\n\\begin{samepage}\n\\noindent\\textbf{", cap, "}\\par\\nobreak\\smallskip\n",
          "\\noindent\\sbox{\\gretablebox}{%\n",
          as.character(table), "\n}%\n",
          "\\ifdim\\wd\\gretablebox>\\linewidth\n",
          "\\resizebox{\\linewidth}{!}{\\usebox{\\gretablebox}}%\n",
          "\\else\\usebox{\\gretablebox}\\fi\\par\n\\end{samepage}\n```\n\n", sep = "")
    }
  } else {
    # Word: plain table; font and table style are applied to the .docx afterwards.
    d[] <- lapply(d, function(col) markdown_text(as.character(col)))
    print(kable(d, format = "pipe", caption = cap, row.names = FALSE, align = align))
  }
  cat("\n\n*Note.* ", markdown_text(gre_table_note(key, params$alpha)), "\n\n", sep = "")
  formulas <- gre_table_math(key)
  if (length(formulas)) cat("**Formulas used**\n\n",
    paste0("$$\n", formulas, "\n$$", collapse = "\n\n"), "\n\n", sep = "")
}
```

}

```{r method-heading, results='asis'}
if (any(vapply(params[c("growth", "trend", "mk", "instab", "decomp", "group_comparison")], has, logical(1))))
  cat("## Methods\n\n")
```

The data are a yearly time series $Y_t$ observed at years $t_1 < t_2 < \dots < t_n$. Each selected numeric series is analysed separately; when a group column is chosen, additive series are first summed over a fixed set of groups for each year. A total is unavailable if any component value is missing. Time is measured as $t = \text{year} - t_1$, so $t = 0$ in the first year.

```{asis, echo = has(params$growth)}
### Growth rates

**Compound growth rate (CGR).** An exponential growth model is fitted to all years by ordinary least squares on the log scale:

$$\ln Y_t = a + b\,t + \varepsilon_t, \qquad \text{CGR}\,(\%) = \left(e^{b} - 1\right) \times 100 .$$

The CGR is the constant annual rate implied by the observed series. The confidence interval transforms both endpoints of the slope t-interval using the same CGR formula. Lag-1 residual correlation is descriptive and uses adjacent calendar years only. Its significance is the $t$-test of $H_0\!: b = 0$ (column *CGR p*). All observed values must be positive and at least three observations are required. The test assumes independent, homoscedastic normal log-scale errors.

**Compound annual growth rate (CAGR).** Uses only the first and last years:

$$\text{CAGR}\,(\%) = \left[\left(\frac{Y_{n}}{Y_{1}}\right)^{1/(t_n - t_1)} - 1\right] \times 100 .$$

Both observed endpoints must be positive. The estimate depends heavily on these two values.

**Average annual growth.** The arithmetic mean of percentage changes between adjacent calendar years with a positive starting value and a nonnegative ending value. Missing years are not bridged.
```

```{asis, echo = has(params$trend)}
### Trend fitting

Four trend models are fitted to each series:

| Model | Equation |
|:--|:--|
| Linear | $Y_t = a + b\,t$ |
| Quadratic | $Y_t = a + b\,t + c\,t^2$ |
| Cubic | $Y_t = a + b\,t + c\,t^2 + d\,t^3$ |
| Exponential | $\ln Y_t = a + b\,t$, i.e. $Y_t = A\,e^{b t}$ |

Models are compared by the small-sample corrected Akaike information criterion (AICc). All likelihoods refer to the observed response scale. Polynomial models use Gaussian errors, and the exponential model uses a lognormal likelihood with the transformation Jacobian. AICc is available when $n > k+1$, where $k$ includes the error variance. The plot shows the fitted mean of the eligible model with the lowest AICc. These are in-sample trends. The likelihood comparison assumes independent observations.
```

```{asis, echo = has(params$mk)}
### Mann-Kendall trend test and Sen's slope

The Mann-Kendall test (Mann, 1945; Kendall, 1975) is a non-parametric test for a monotonic trend; it does not assume a straight line or normally distributed errors. The test statistic is

$$S = \sum_{i=1}^{n-1}\sum_{j=i+1}^{n} \operatorname{sgn}\left(Y_j - Y_i\right),$$

with variance, corrected for $g$ groups of tied values of size $t_p$,

$$\operatorname{Var}(S) = \frac{n(n-1)(2n+5) - \sum_{p=1}^{g} t_p (t_p - 1)(2 t_p + 5)}{18}.$$

The standardised statistic is $Z = (S - 1)/\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(S)}$ if $S > 0$, $Z = 0$ if $S = 0$ and $Z = (S + 1)/\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(S)}$ if $S < 0$, with a two-sided $p$-value from the standard normal distribution. Kendall's tau-b adjusts for ties in the response and is undefined for a constant series. For fewer than 10 observations without ties, the app uses an exact two-sided p-value.

**Sen's slope** (Sen, 1968) is the median of all pairwise slopes, $Q = \operatorname{median}\left\{(Y_j - Y_i)/(t_j - t_i) : i < j\right\}$, a robust estimate of the change per year in the units of the series. Its confidence interval uses the ordered slopes at ranks $(N - C_\alpha)/2$ and $(N + C_\alpha)/2$, where $N$ is the number of pairs and $C_\alpha = z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(S)}$.

The test assumes independent yearly observations. Serial correlation can affect p-values and intervals. The reported p-values are per series and are unadjusted for multiple testing.
```

```{asis, echo = has(params$instab)}
### Instability

The coefficient of variation, $\text{CV}\,(\%) = s / \bar Y \times 100$, measures total variability, including the part caused by the trend itself. The Cuddy-Della Valle Index (Cuddy and Della Valle, 1978) removes the trend using the adjusted $\bar R^2$ of the linear trend:

$$\text{CDVI}\,(\%) = \text{CV} \times \sqrt{1 - \bar R^2}.$$

The adjusted R-squared is bounded below at zero so a poor fit does not increase the index above the CV. Both measures require nonnegative observations and a positive mean.
```

```{asis, echo = has(params$decomp)}
### Area-yield decomposition

Production is area times yield, $P = A \times Y$, with yield computed as $P/A$. The change between the first (0) and last (1) year is split additively:

$$\Delta P = \underbrace{Y_0\,\Delta A}_{\text{area effect}} + \underbrace{A_0\,\Delta Y}_{\text{yield effect}} + \underbrace{\Delta A\,\Delta Y}_{\text{interaction}},$$

so the three effects add up to the total change in production. Percentage shares are undefined when the total change is zero. The decomposition describes accounting contributions and does not identify causal effects.
```

```{asis, echo = has(params$group_comparison)}
### Group comparisons

Growth rates are estimated separately for each group and for the combined annual series. Combined derived yield is total production divided by total area in the source units. Group intervals are individual model intervals and do not test differences between groups.
```

}

Generated with RAISINS (R & AI Solutions in INferential Statistics). Methods: compound growth rate (log-linear regression), CAGR, polynomial/exponential trend fitting, the non-parametric Mann-Kendall test with Sen's slope, the Cuddy-Della Valle instability index, and additive area-yield decomposition of production.
